portrait-agnes-hobday.webp.prompt:
A character portrait in a painterly fantasy-realism style, the classic CRPG portrait look: head and shoulders, three-quarter view, looking at the viewer, dramatic soft key light, a dark, softly painted background. No text, lettering, borders or frames.

Federation art direction: brutalism. Monumental raw-concrete masses, heavy slabs and deep-set windows, stark repeated geometry and hard shadows, grey and white with heraldic banners and crests; architecture built to dwarf the people in it, ordered, imposing and austere.

Art bible for the Merrow system. Palette: olive green, deep sea blue, pale slate grey, ochre, slate grey and sand. Lighting: Warm, low yellow sunlight over wet land, soft cloud shadow rolling across fields, hard pale light on grey stonework. Dusk brings warm window lights and distant lightning. Moons are lit flat and ashen under a black sky, with the blue-and-white arc of Merrow hanging over them. Architecture: Monumental and symmetrical: long granary blocks like barracks, farm domes laid out in strict grids, river quays with stepped stone wharves, processing cities built in ranks along the rivers. Heraldic crests and numbered bays mark every gate. On the moons, domes and container stacks sit in disciplined rows on bare rock. Materials: Poured grey concrete, pale composite panels, glazed dome lattices, painted steel cranes, white-stencilled numbers on grey. Soil, straw, grain dust and river mud blur the edges of every clean surface. Mood: Comfortable and orderly, a little complacent, with a new undercurrent of strain: full storehouses and crowded warehouses, tired officers, a lot of people waiting patiently. Design language: Federation design: disciplined, symmetrical, armoured. Grey and white with heraldic markings, numbered bays and crests, heavy plain geometry. Even farm sheds look like fortifications, and uniforms and work coats alike carry insignia and rank stripes.

Agnes Hobday, grain factor, at Merrow Fields (Merrow). A broad woman in her sixties with a sunburnt face and iron-grey plait, wearing a canvas coat with a harvest-board badge. A grain-weigher's brass gauge hangs from her belt, polished by constant use.

Who they are: A river-barge factor who has sold Merrow's harvest to every system in the March. She knows what each hold wants and what each master will pay for it, and she is wary of anyone who asks about the evacuees.

Their people: Merrow people are plain-spoken, early-rising and proud of their hands. They judge strangers by whether they know what a good loaf is, and they talk about weather the way other systems talk about money. Federal rule is simply the way things are: the navy is the landlord, the harvest board is the church, and a crest on a gate is respectable. They are generous to evacuees in practice and wary in conversation, since the camps eat from the same stores. Ironhull crews are called ore-eaters, mostly with affection. Prism associates are treated as polite weather. Anyone who complains about the levy does so at home, with the door shut and the radio on.

The background is the dim bar of the port, out of focus, in the system's palette.

Art bible for the Merrow system. Palette: olive green, deep sea blue, pale slate grey, ochre, slate grey and sand. Lighting: Warm, low yellow sunlight over wet land, soft cloud shadow rolling across fields, hard pale light on grey stonework. Dusk brings warm window lights and distant lightning. Moons are lit flat and ashen under a black sky, with the blue-and-white arc of Merrow hanging over them. Architecture: Monumental and symmetrical: long granary blocks like barracks, farm domes laid out in strict grids, river quays with stepped stone wharves, processing cities built in ranks along the rivers. Heraldic crests and numbered bays mark every gate. On the moons, domes and container stacks sit in disciplined rows on bare rock. Materials: Poured grey concrete, pale composite panels, glazed dome lattices, painted steel cranes, white-stencilled numbers on grey. Soil, straw, grain dust and river mud blur the edges of every clean surface. Mood: Comfortable and orderly, a little complacent, with a new undercurrent of strain: full storehouses and crowded warehouses, tired officers, a lot of people waiting patiently. Design language: Federation design: disciplined, symmetrical, armoured. Grey and white with heraldic markings, numbered bays and crests, heavy plain geometry. Even farm sheds look like fortifications, and uniforms and work coats alike carry insignia and rank stripes.

The place: Merrow Fields, the agri port of Merrow. One of the most crowded places in the region, home to billions: city to the horizon, towers and lights everywhere, the sky busy with ships. Merrow is a water world: deep sea blue seas, green lowlands and olive highlands with snow on the peaks, under drifting white cloud; its sky is pale sky blue, and its settlements show warm lights at dusk, with lightning in its storms. The light comes from a yellow star.

The scene: Seen from the landing field at late afternoon: white-lined pads in the foreground, then a long grey granary with a crest above its doors and a number on its roof. Beyond it lie green lowlands and rows of farm domes climbing olive highlands with snow on the peaks, under drifting white cloud and a pale blue sky. The yellow star sits low and warm, a river catches the light, and the first window lights glow at dusk.
